newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT-Blue Square rated buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Blue Square rated buy.

text.p: UBS said Blue Square shares traded on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange offer a strong arbitrage opportunity as they are trading at a large discount to its parent, traded on the New York Stock Exchange.

UBS's director of Israel research Daniel Carasso said in a report that the U.S. shares are still cheap and are rated a buy despite the 35 percent appreciation since the initial public offering in July.

"However during this time the price of BSI's (Blue Square Israel) TASE-traded subsidiary BSCIP has been flat; it now stands on a 35 percent lower rating than BSI. As the constituent parts of BSI and BSCIP overlap so much this represents a seemingly inexplicable valuation anomaly offering a clear buying/arbitrage opportunity," the report said.
Blue Square Israel's main assets are 66 percent of Blue Square Chain Israel Investments & Properties (BSCIP) and 90 supermarkets.
The subsidiary's sale/profits are 65 percent food-led hypermarkets and 35 percent Hamashbir, Israel's largest department store chain.

The parent company has a greater food retailing focus, a more liquid quote and better disclosure while the subsidiary offers greater exposure to the larger hypermarkets, no IPO dilution in 1996-97 and, as a result, faster earnings per share growth, the report said.
"BSCIP now trades at a 35 percent discount to BSI in P/E terms, apparantly for no other reason than that the TASE is still something very far from an efficient market," the report said.
Carasso said BSCIP is also trading at a 100 percent valuation discount to international comparables.
"We consider BSCIP to be the cheapest equity we are aware of on the TASE. We continue to rate BSCIP an aggressive buy," the report said.
